query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Changing the percentage of elements in HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy (HEA) will significantly affect its mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with a specific composition.
generation.intervention: Varying the elemental percentages of Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in the HEA.
generation.conditions: Controlled environment with consistent temperature and pressure during alloy processing.
generation.structural_mediator: The atomic arrangement and bonding characteristics of the HEA.
generation.mechanism: Alterations in elemental percentages will lead to changes in phase stability, grain structure, and dislocation behavior, thereby affecting mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Mechanical properties such as yield strength, ductility, and hardness will vary with different compositions of the HEA.
generation.baseline: Initial mechanical properties of the HEA at a standard composition.
generation.boundary: The study is limited to the HfNbTaTiZr HEA and does not extend to other HEAs or alloys.
generation.uncertainty: The specific quantitative relationship between elemental percentages and mechanical properties is not established.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of mechanical tests on HfNbTaTiZr HEA samples with systematically varied elemental percentages.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant changes in mechanical properties are observed with varying elemental percentages, the hypothesis is falsified.
